session.vm: innovacx-vm (GCP europe-west1-b, 34.38.76.62 internal, accessed via IAP tunnel)

root_cause.summary: The GitHub Actions self-hosted CI runner runs on the same GCP VM as the live production Docker stack. Both used the same Docker Compose project name ('innova-cx'). Every CI merge-gate run executed 'docker compose down -v --remove-orphans' which wiped the live innova-cx_postgres_data volume. PostgreSQL then re-initialised with CI seed credentials (APP_DB_PASSWORD=changeme123) while the VM .env had a different password — causing all backend services to fail with 'password authentication failed for user innovacx_app' on every restart.
secondary_causes: uvicorn --reload in production caused periodic backend restarts (~every 15s) explaining the page refresh
ML container health check start_period too short — Docker declared them unhealthy before models loaded, triggering restart loops
nginx redirect loop: GCP LB forwards all traffic (including HTTPS user requests) to the VM on port 80 as plain HTTP. nginx redirected port 80 → HTTPS, creating an infinite redirect loop
GCP LB health check (/api/health on port 80) was being routed to the frontend (port 5173) which returned 404, permanently marking the backend as unhealthy
Three.js loaded from external CDN (cdnjs.cloudflare.com) — no fallback if CDN fails or WebGL unavailable

fixes.title: Remove uvicorn --reload from production
fixes.problem: backend/entrypoint.sh ran uvicorn with --reload flag and docker-compose.yml set WATCHFILES_FORCE_POLLING=true. In production this caused the backend to restart every ~15 seconds (watchfiles polling triggered restarts), explaining the page refresh.

docker-compose.yml.after: removed entirely (replaced by Google OAuth env vars that were added in a recent merge)

fixes.title: Fix ML container health check start_period
fixes.problem: ML containers (chatbot, transcriber, orchestrator) had start_period too short. Docker declared them unhealthy before models finished loading, triggering Docker's restart policy in a tight crash loop.

fixes.title: Fix GCP Load Balancer health check routing
fixes.problem: GCP LB sends 'GET /api/health HTTP/1.1' to port 80 on the VM with Host: 10.0.2.2 (internal IP, not innovacx.net). nginx had no default server block — all port 80 traffic went to the first server block which proxied everything to port 5173 (the frontend). Frontend has no /api/health endpoint → 404 → LB marks backend UNHEALTHY → serves 'no healthy upstream' to all users.
files_changed: /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/lb-health (NEW FILE, on VM only — not in git)
fixes.result: LB health check now hits backend:8000 directly and gets HTTP 200. Backend marked HEALTHY within 10 seconds.
fixes.note: This file is on the VM's nginx config only, not tracked in git. If VM is recreated it must be re-applied.

fixes.title: Fix nginx redirect loop caused by GCP LB
fixes.problem: GCP LB terminates SSL and forwards ALL traffic (including user HTTPS requests) to the VM backend on port 80 as plain HTTP. The nginx innovacx.net port 80 block was doing 'return 301 https://$host$request_uri'. The LB forwarded this 301 back to the VM as another port 80 request → infinite redirect loop → Firefox showed 'The page isn't redirecting properly'.
fixes.before: server { listen 80; server_name innovacx.net www.innovacx.net; return 301 https://$host$request_uri; }
fixes.after: server { listen 80; server_name innovacx.net www.innovacx.net; [all location blocks — /api/ → 8000, /chatbot/ → 8001, /whisper/ → 3001, / → 5173] }
fixes.explanation: With GCP LB in front, HTTPS is terminated at the LB. The VM backend only needs to serve HTTP on port 80. The LB enforces HTTPS at the edge. The VM must NOT redirect HTTP → HTTPS or it creates a loop.
fixes.note: This file is on the VM's nginx config only, not tracked in git. If VM is recreated it must be re-applied.

fixes.title: Serve Three.js locally instead of CDN
fixes.problem: PublicLanding.jsx loaded Three.js dynamically from 'https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/ajax/libs/three.js/r128/three.min.js'. If CDN is unreachable or slow, the solar system never initialises and the page splash screen hangs indefinitely.

frontend/src/pages/PublicLanding.jsx.after: const THREE_CDN = "/three.min.js"; // served locally — no CDN dependency

fixes.note: three.min.js is now in frontend/public/ and gets copied to dist/ during vite build. Served at /three.min.js by the vite preview server.

fixes.title: Add splash screen fallback timeout and WebGL error handling
fixes.problem: The PublicLanding splash screen required TWO conditions to clear: (1) 2.8s timer AND (2) Three.js WebGL fires onReady() after first animation frame. If WebGL was unavailable or Three.js failed for any reason, the splash hung forever showing a black screen.

frontend/src/pages/PublicLanding.jsx — s.before: const t = setTimeout(() => { splashDoneRef.current = true; if (readyRef.current) setReady(true); }, 2800); return () => clearTimeout(t);
frontend/src/pages/PublicLanding.jsx — s.after: const t = setTimeout(() => { splashDoneRef.current = true; if (readyRef.current) setReady(true); }, 2800); const fallback = setTimeout(() => { readyRef.current = true; splashDoneRef.current = true; setReady(true); }, 6000); return () => { clearTimeout(t); clearTimeout(fallback); };

frontend/src/pages/PublicLanding.jsx — W.description: Wrapped script.onload in try/catch. If THREE.WebGLRenderer throws (WebGL unavailable), adds CSS class 'pl-solar-fallback' to the canvas container and calls onReady() so the splash still clears.
frontend/src/pages/PublicLanding.jsx — W.after: script.onload = () => { try { init(); } catch (err) { console.warn('[SolarSystem] WebGL unavailable, using CSS fallback:', err.message); if (mount) mount.classList.add('pl-solar-fallback'); onReady && onReady(); } }; script.onerror = () => { console.warn('[SolarSystem] Failed to load three.min.js, using CSS fallback'); if (mount) mount.classList.add('pl-solar-fallback'); onReady && onReady(); };

frontend/src/pages/PublicLanding.css — W.description: Added .pl-solar-fallback CSS class that shows animated concentric orbit rings using box-shadow and keyframe animations. Shown only when WebGL context creation fails (e.g. hardware acceleration disabled in browser).

architecture_notes.gcp_lb: GCP Global Load Balancer at 35.244.136.89 terminates SSL. Forwards all traffic (HTTP and HTTPS) to the VM on port 80 as plain HTTP. VM nginx must NOT redirect port 80 → HTTPS or it creates a redirect loop.
architecture_notes.firewall: Only ports 22, 80, 443 are open externally. Ports 8000 (backend), 8001 (chatbot), 8004 (orchestrator), 5173 (frontend) are accessible only via nginx proxy on the VM.
architecture_notes.ci_runner: Self-hosted GitHub Actions runner runs on the same VM as production. Always use COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=innovacx-ci in CI workflows to isolate from the live innova-cx Docker project.
architecture_notes.db_init: postgres_data volume only runs init scripts on FIRST START (fresh volume). If volume already exists Docker skips init entirely. To force reinit: docker compose down, docker volume rm innova-cx_postgres_data, then bring postgres back up.
architecture_notes.frontend_build: Frontend runs as 'vite preview' (production static build) inside Docker. Build takes ~60s. During this time port 5173 is down and the GCP LB will mark the backend unhealthy. This is expected — the lb-health nginx block ensures /api/health still responds during frontend rebuilds.
